subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): expose anonymous Talk activity to plugins

question: Should every installed plugin receive anonymous activity from every Talk session, or must process-wide observation be restricted by an explicit Plugin SDK capability, owner scope, or operator grant?
rationale: The branch intentionally removed the earlier grant-based designs, and source evidence cannot determine whether universal cross-session metadata is the repository's intended long-term plugin trust contract.

options.title: Require explicit observation authority
options.body: Restore an enforced manifest capability, owner scope, or operator-approved entitlement before forwarding the shared feed to a plugin.

options.title: Ratify universal plugin access
options.body: Keep the current implementation and document that all installed plugins may observe anonymous process-wide Talk activity and its metadata limits.

options.title: Defer the public API
options.body: Pause this new SDK surface until the broader Talk plugin trust model is decided alongside the managed-session work.

recommendation.title: Require explicit observation authority
recommendation.body: Restore an enforced manifest capability, owner scope, or operator-approved entitlement before forwarding the shared feed to a plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the most evidenced recent contributor to the adjacent Talk architecture and this proposed SDK contract; core owners can join that decision through normal review.
